title: Titus 3: renovation by the Spirit opposed to works of righteousness we did
source_text: XXXIX. Adde quod Apostolus ultimo illo loco, ex epistola ad Titum desumpto, non vult operibus justitiae tribui, id quod tribuendum est renovationi per Spiritum Sanctum. Salvos, inquit, nos fecit, non ex operibus justitiae quae fecerimus nos, sed per lavacrum regenerationis & renovationis Spiritus Sancti. Unde sequitur nostram sanctificationem, quae per lavacrum illud regenerationis, & spiritum renovantem in nobis peragitur, ex sensu Pauli non debere dici ex operibus justitiae quae nos fecerimus. Quandoquidem opposita sunt, aliquid per spiritus renovationem fieri, & esse ex operibus justitiae quae fecimus nos.
pass_a_gloss: Add that the Apostle in that last place taken from the epistle to Titus does not wish that to be attributed to works of righteousness which is to be attributed to renovation through the Holy Spirit. He saved us, he says, not of works of righteousness which we have done, but through the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit. Whence it follows that our sanctification, which is wrought in us through that washing of regeneration and the renewing Spirit, according to Paul's sense ought not to be said to be of works of righteousness which we have done. Since they are opposite: that something be done through the Spirit's renovation, and that it be of works of righteousness which we have done.
pass_b_english: Titus 3: Spirit's renovating wash—not works of righteousness we did—is the saving means.
Therefore sanctification itself must not be called of our righteous works.

lemmas.gloss: to renovation through the Holy Spirit
